One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.\\n\\nThe hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.\\n\\nState is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.\\n\\nBrian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.\\n\\nSound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.\\n\\nTickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. An Owed line's ticket goes to Todo with a comment saying what is owed and who has it. Leave the Delivered and Ready ones as they are.\\n\\nSharing: both files, view only. Everyone on the kickoff hold, and PlayableX through their intake address, which is in Contacts.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_8c1d0bca1d1d5fde4c5008", "title": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes", "name": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes", "revisionId": "5ddbee1c86", "createdTime": "2025-09-30T16:25:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-30T16:58:19Z", "text": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes

The brief. One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.

The hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.

State is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.

Brian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.

Sound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.

Tickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. An Owed line's ticket goes to Todo with a comment saying what is owed and who has it. Leave the Delivered and Ready ones as they are.

Sharing: both files, view only. Everyone on the kickoff hold, and PlayableX through their intake address, which is in Contacts.
"}

2025-09-29T19:42:05Z Frederick Stone [r=1 ts=1759174925.309129] <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> we are considering a pretty substantial pivot in core game play for Zombie Match. I think we should pause development of the playable for a month or so to make sure we aren't building something that doesn't align with the game's ultimate aesthetic or core game play. Does that work on your end?

2025-09-18T20:28:08Z Frederick Stone [r=15 ts=1758227288.370029] <@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID> can you help package up assets? <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> can you help [PERSON_NAME_0092] narrow down what is needed? Any examples you could share of specifically what you're after would be helpful.

2025-09-12T16:38:28Z Frederick Stone [r=4 ts=1757695108.506159] Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, the way I see it, playables can be good for optimizing for CPIs (fun casual playable but unrelated to core game), optimizing for retention (filter out users that are not going to like your game), or somewhere in the middle. I think Scenario 1 is a good bet for filtering out the players that won't like our game, while remaining true to our core game play.  For Scenario 1, would the user be able to select any items they want and make several matches (if they are good enough)? I like that idea -- but will call out it seems a lot more sophisticated than the Domino Delights playable where the user is essentially on rails and only makes a few matches before the playable ends.

2025-09-03T18:46:53Z Leonard Hayes [r=0 ts=1756925213.271559] hey guys, sorry we are silent - some product work took priority - we’ll circle back with you as soon as we can

2025-09-01T17:46:58Z Leonard Hayes [r=0 ts=1756748818.259249] Hi, the entire product team is out today (in Turkey we observe the Aug 30th and in the US we have a long weekend). We’ll circle back with you over the next day or two. Thank you for the follow up!

2025-09-01T14:02:04Z PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID [r=0 ts=1756735324.206019] Hi <!here>, Have you been able to make a clear decision about our ideas? What direction should we take with the scenario? Do you have any suggestions in addition to the scenarios we've prepared?

2025-08-29T07:25:58Z PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID [r=0 ts=1756452358.461719] Hello <!here>, thank you for your valuable feedback! As <@EMPLOYEE_0012_SLACK_ID> mentioned, if we use a character it will strengthen all scenarios and help players build an emotional connection. If you already have a character, we can integrate it into all scenarios.  If you have a preferred scenario in mind, we’re happy to consider that as well. Our suggestion, however, is to move forward with *Scenario 1 and highlight the basic gameplay*. Presenting the game in its simplest and most authentic form allows players to clearly understand the core mechanic. This way, they can evaluate the game more accurately, and your first tests will deliver much cleaner results.  In short, *a simple playable = strong first impression + clear mechanic focus + lower drop-off*, which ultimately means more reliable test outcomes.

2025-08-28T18:00:56Z Vincent Parker [r=0 ts=1756404056.404979] I also liked the third option, but my only concern is that it might not be as exciting as the other two since we don't have an avatar to associate with.

{"ts": "1758911910.876289", "type": "message", "text": "I’ve been playing Archero 2 and <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io> for a while, and I’ve developed some theories about how levels and monsters work in these games
• In Archero 2, the Arena usually uses a fixed set of monster types. These monsters are presented to the player in different sequences, creating variation across levels. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player’s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you’re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.
    ◦ Another thing I’m confident about is that the monsters’ HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. A monster you encounter at Level 1 will appear again at Level 45, but with boosted stats. This scaling seems to be the game’s way of balancing the player’s increasing strength.
• In <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io>, I don’t think monsters’ individual stats scale the same way. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you’re suddenly dealing with 100. 2025-09-26T18:38:30Z Brian Foster [r=0 ts=1758911910.876289] I’ve been playing Archero 2 and <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io> for a while, and I’ve developed some theories about how levels and monsters work in these games • In Archero 2, the Arena usually uses a fixed set of monster types. These monsters are presented to the player in different sequences, creating variation across levels. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player’s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you’re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.     ◦ Another thing I’m confident about is that the monsters’ HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. A monster you encounter at Level 1 will appear again at Level 45, but with boosted stats. This scaling seems to be the game’s way of balancing the player’s increasing strength. • In <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io>, I don’t think monsters’ individual stats scale the same way. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you’re suddenly dealing with 100. This makes their cumulative attack power the real challenge

2025-09-26T18:38:30Z Brian Foster [r=0 ts=1758911910.876289] I’ve been playing Archero 2 and <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io> for a while, and I’ve developed some theories about how levels and monsters work in these games • In Archero 2, the Arena usually uses a fixed set of monster types. These monsters are presented to the player in different sequences, creating variation across levels. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player’s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you’re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.     ◦ Another thing I’m confident about is that the monsters’ HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. A monster you encounter at Level 1 will appear again at Level 45, but with boosted stats. This scaling seems to be the game’s way of balancing the player’s increasing strength. • In <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io>, I don’t think monsters’ individual stats scale the same way. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you’re suddenly dealing with 100. This makes their cumulative attack power the real challenge

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_zm3d_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Zombie Match 3D \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

This is the living Game Design Document for Zombie Match 3D (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies under Calm Play LLC until the transfer to Harmony Games and the rename on 24 July 2025). It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. For the coin/life economy see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters, and for the paid track see ZM3D Season Pass - Spec. This document ladders up to Product OKRs - 2025 H1.

ZM3D has not had a global launch. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025; May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live. This GDD reflects that build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match it counts as a blunder: the tray clears and surviving monsters enrage, but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state - the loss screen only appears at zero health. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics - objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.
  • 7-slot tray - the primary tempo penalty, not the fail state; tuning slot count changes felt difficulty more than object count.
  • Object families - cosmetic skins that map to elemental ammo in the RPG layer.

Zombie RPG layer

Levels wrap the matcher in combat. Each cleared triple fires the matching element at the current monster. Monsters carry an elemental weakness; hitting the weakness deals bonus damage and can apply a status.

Monster / element table

The roster is an everyday-people theme rather than classic undead. Minion families scale in tiers; bosses come in standard, Fast and Turbo variants.

FamilyTypeTiers
PunkMinion1-5
BikerMinion1-4
KarenMinion1-4
AfroMinion1-3
Riot Police, Chef, Scientist, Fire Fighter, Magician, Librarian, Tech Bro, Gym Bro, Baseball Player, CheerleaderMinionin development
VarC-Mayor1 250 / VarC-Mayor2 225 / VarC-Chef 175 (base HP, scaled at runtime; the older 180/300/500 prefabs are retired)Bossstandard, Fast, Turbo

Elemental weaknesses used by boosters and abilities: shock, poison, burn, freeze, splash, stun, blind. Glue is a booster, not an element.

Modes

  • Campaign - authored levels, escalating monster mixes.
  • Endless - survival board with an item refill every 30s to keep the pile stocked.
  • Infinite-HP Boss - a damage-race against a boss whose HP does not deplete to zero; the score is total damage dealt before the tray fills.

Monetization

The headline product is the Season Pass at $6.99, reached production in the week of September 22-29, 2025. It runs a free and a premium reward track over a fixed season window; progression is earned through campaign and Endless play. Coin, life, and booster sinks live in the linked Economy doc - do not duplicate values here.

Known launch issues (tracked, historical):

  • Hard crash from consecutive glass-impact SFX/VFX on Android, mostly Samsung (Aug-Sep 2025, ZOM-475), fixed by removing the glass SFX and VFX. The separate addressables splash-hang belongs to Domino Delights.
  • The font-download freeze that stalls the splash screen at ~22% on slow connections is also Domino Delights (ENG-2346, May 2025); the ZM3D client has no remote font download.

Boss mode reward config

Owner: Robert (Product). Design: Julia Lawson. Changes to tray count or refill cadence must be reviewed against the OKR dashboard before shipping.

input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX

Game: Zombie Match 3D (Puzzles vs Zombies on the stores)
Written: 1 October 2025, for the game as it is today. We are looking at a change to the core gameplay. If it happens, we will go through the affected parts of this brief with you again in November, before or at the kickoff.

1. Start date
Kickoff is Monday 3 November 2025, the date you are holding for us. The project is paused until then.

2. Scenario
We picked Scenario 1, the core-mechanic playable. It is there for retention, not cheap installs: show the game the way it really plays, so players who won't enjoy it filter themselves out and the ones who install know what they are getting. The player chooses freely which items to tap and can keep making matches for as long as they are good enough. This is not on rails like the Domino Delights playable.

3. How a level plays
- Items sit in a pile on the board. The player taps items to move them into a tray at the bottom.
- The tray has 7 slots. When 3 matching items are in the tray they clear, and the matched item is fired at the zombies (the rocket launcher, our Cannon asset, does the firing).
- Zombies walk toward the player. Each item type hits them differently (for example the grenade is powerful, the couch does splash damage, the plushie is weak but funny).
- If all 7 tray slots fill without a match, that is a blunder: the tray clears and the zombies still standing get enraged, but play goes on. A full tray is NOT a loss.
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach the player and the player's HP runs out (zero health). That is the only fail condition.
- Background: the background of the reference level (sent in the first zip, 24 Sep).
Reference: the level we built for you on 23 Sep, which Brian recorded and sent on 24 Sep.

4. The board: eight items
These eight are the default set on the board:
1. Grenade
2. Couch
3. Plushie Chick (the one you called the duck)
4. Shuriken
5. Cute Axe
6. Gift Box
7. Cactus Plant
8. Bow
Every other board item on our pack list is an extra you can make swappable on the platform, so we can test other items later. Note: Bow replaced Dynamite in the eight on 26 Sep. Dynamite is now an extra.

5. Zombies and animation
- Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player. All four are in the Unity pack we sent on 26 Sep.
- One animation for all four: walk.
- We may add more zombies in a later stage, as you suggested.

6. Sound
What you can use:
- Matching sound, success sound and failure sound: made in-house, yours to use.
- Background music: a new track made for the ad (not the in-game music). It is still being cut down to a loop and will come from us.
What is still coming:
- Rocket sound and explosion sound: the versions we have come from a sound library and a bought pack, so we cannot hand them over. We will send our own versions. If copies of them already reached you, please do not use them.
Music rule (your rule from the Domino playable, still applies): the music may only start after the player's first tap.

7. Formats (as you told us, still holds)
- 3D: .fbx, .glb or .blend. FBX exported in Binary, not ASCII.
- 2D: .png (2D animated characters split into parts).
- Fonts: .ttf or .woff2.
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav.

8. What is still coming from us
The hand-off list shows every line of the pack: what you already have (Delivered), what is exported and waiting in our outgoing folder (Ready), and what we still owe and who on our side has it (Owed). It is shared with you alongside this brief.

Contacts on our side: Frederick Stone (project), Julia Lawson (brief and design), Brian Foster (assets), Robert (game design).

Done. Both files are in my Drive and shared view-only with you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake.
• Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/5aaa92042d2f73f189934fb3/edit
• Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BBT5u-IuGF0cK-0Fji72F4FxGm89a-KTvMMD2fL3-pI/edit

Count by state, across all 96 lines of Brian's pack list:
• *Delivered: 8.* Couch, Couch and Pillow, Grenade, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick, Cannon, Background, Zombie characters.
• *Ready: 68.* Exported, current and in the outgoing folder.
• *Owed: 20.*
   ◦ Claire, 9: FBXs for Fly Zapper, Fire Extinguisher, Beach Ball, Rubber Ducky, Grand Piano and Wheelbarrow. Re-exports for Chainsaw, Cone and Cactus Plant.
   ◦ Brian, 7: exports for Propane Tank, Toy Train, Small Kettle, Tall Kettle and Wooden Crate, plus item visuals and UI PNGs from Figma.
   ◦ Calvin, 3: our own rocket and explosion sounds, and the music loop.
   ◦ Martin, 1: fonts.

What changed from Brian's notes:
• Robert put Bow into the eight in place of Dynamite (26 Sep, #zombie-art). The board is now Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant and Bow.
• Chainsaw, Cone and Cactus Plant got new colour versions after their 25 Sep export (Claire's PR #462), so they have to go again. Cactus is one of the eight.
• Calvin's sound sources sheet says the rocket sound is from Soundly and the explosion is from a bought Asset Store pack. Both are sitting in the outgoing folder and need pulling until we have our own.

The 20 Owed tickets are in Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it. Delivered and Ready tickets are unchanged. The brief describes the game as it plays today, and I've flagged that we'll redo the affected parts in November if the core changes.

Hi team, ahead of the 3 November kickoff, here are the two files for the ZM3D playable:
• *Brief* (what to build from): https://docs.google.com/document/d/5aaa92042d2f73f189934fb3/edit
• *Hand-off list* (every asset line and its state): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BBT5u-IuGF0cK-0Fji72F4FxGm89a-KTvMMD2fL3-pI/edit

Short version:
• Scenario 1.
• The 8 board items: Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant, Bow. Bow has replaced Dynamite. Every other board item is a swappable extra.
• The 4 zombies are Party Girl, Plumber, Magician and Football Player, all with the walk animation only.
• The tray has 7 slots. A full tray is a penalty, not a loss. You lose only when the zombies reach you and HP runs out, and you win when every zombie on screen is gone.
• Music starts only after the first tap.

The list shows what you already have (Delivered), what's exported and waiting on our side (Ready), and what we still owe (Owed). 20 lines are still owed, including the rocket and explosion sounds, background music, fonts, 2D item visuals and UI, and a few FBXs. If you already have copies of the rocket or explosion sound, please don't use them; we'll send our own versions.

The brief describes the game as it plays today. If our core gameplay changes before November, we'll go through the affected parts with you then.

content.text:
I've done everything Frederick asked for in his Sep 30 message: the brief and the hand-off list are in your Drive, the tickets are updated, and the links are posted in the PlayableX channel.

**Files** (view-only for Frederick, Brian, Robert and intake@playablex.ai, the PlayableX address from Contacts):
- Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/5aaa92042d2f73f189934fb3/edit
- Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BBT5u-IuGF0cK-0Fji72F4FxGm89a-KTvMMD2fL3-pI/edit

**Counts** (sent to Frederick in your DM with him), across all 96 lines of Brian's pack list:
- **Delivered: 8.** Couch, Couch and Pillow, Grenade, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick, Cannon, Background, Zombie characters.
- **Ready: 68.** Exported, current and sitting in the outgoing folder.
- **Owed: 20.**
  - Claire, 9: six FBXs still to make, plus re-exports of Chainsaw, Cone and Cactus Plant.
  - Brian, 7: five exports, plus item visuals and UI as PNGs from Figma.
  - Calvin, 3: our own rocket and explosion sounds, and the music loop.
  - Martin, 1: fonts.

**Where things differ from Brian's ticket notes:**
- **Board line-up:** On Sep 26 in #zombie-art, Robert put Bow into the eight in place of Dynamite. The eight are now Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant and Bow. Dynamite is an extra.
- **Re-exports:** Claire's GitHub PR #462 added new colour versions of the Chainsaw, Cone and Cactus Plant after Brian exported them on Sep 25, so those files are out of date. Cactus is one of the eight.
- **Sounds:** Calvin's "ZM3D sound sources" sheet shows the rocket sound comes from a sound library and the explosion from a bought pack, so neither can go to PlayableX. Brian's notes had them in the outgoing folder. Someone needs to take them out until Calvin's own versions exist; I noted that on both tickets.

**Brief contents:** It covers what Frederick's notes asked for:
- Scenario 1, and that it's meant to filter for players who'll stay.
- The eight board items, with every other board item as a swappable extra.
- The four zombies (Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player) with walk only.
- Win and lose rules: win when every zombie is gone, lose only when HP runs out. The 7-slot tray filling up is a penalty, not a loss.
- Which sounds they can use, and their own rule that music starts only after the first tap.
- Their file formats and the Nov 3 start date.

It describes the game as it plays today and says we'll redo the affected parts in November if the core changes.

**Tickets:** The 20 Owed tickets are moved to Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it. The Delivered and Ready tickets are unchanged.

**Slack:** The PlayableX channel post has both links, a short summary, and the list of what's still coming from us.
